GK-06.c01: A safe driver knows what is happening **all around** the vehicle, ahead, beside and behind.
Poor looking habits are a **major cause of crashes**.
GK-06.c02: Look **12 to 15 seconds or more** ahead, because a big vehicle needs a lot of distance to stop or change lanes.
12–15 seconds ahead is about **one block** at lower (city) speeds and about **a quarter of a mile** at highway speeds.
Look for the 2 main things ahead, **traffic** and **road conditions**, and move your eyes back and forth, near and far.
A **"stale" green light** (green for a long while) will likely change before you get there → begin to slow and prepare to stop.
GK-06.c03: [CA] California-registered vehicles need **2 or more mirrors**, one on the left, showing the road behind for **200 feet or more** (CVC §26709).
Check mirrors with quick glances; don't stare. In a **convex** mirror, things look **smaller and farther away** than they really are.
Check mirror adjustment before every trip, **only with the trailer(s) straight**, so each mirror shows part of your own vehicle as a reference point.
Check mirrors more in 4 situations: turns, merges, tight maneuvers, and lane changes, which need **4 checks** (before, after signaling, right after starting, after finishing).
GK-06.c04: Communicating means **signaling your intentions**, telling others what you are going to do.
It also means **communicating your presence**, making sure others know you are there.
GK-06.c05: Turn signals follow **3 rules**: signal early, signal continuously until the turn is finished, and cancel the signal afterward.
Signaling early is the **most effective way** to stop others from trying to pass you.
To warn of slowing, **tap the brake pedal lightly** so the brake lights blink; save the **4-way flashers** for very slow driving or when stopped.
**Do not direct traffic** by waving others past, because it could cause a crash and the blame could fall on you.
GK-06.c06: When passing, **assume others have not seen you**; tap the horn lightly, or after dark flash headlights low → high → low.
At dawn, dusk, rain or snow, turn on your **headlights on low beam**; clearance lights alone are not enough.
Stopped at the roadside, use **4-way flashers** and don't rely on taillights; set out warning devices **within 10 minutes**.
Divided or one-way road → triangles at **10, 100 and 200 feet** behind; two-lane road → within **10 feet** of a corner, 100 feet behind, 100 feet ahead.
If a hill or curve hides you within **500 feet**, move the rear triangle back beyond it; carry triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
